# Landscape: factories x components

How other products handle the components covered in lesson 1: whether a person approves or edits the plan first,
whether the plan becomes tasks that outlive the chat, whether those tasks carry criteria and dependencies,
what judges a task done, whether the loop moves on to the next task by itself, and who drives that loop. Each cell is
a paraphrase of a first-party page, with its source URL and the date it was fetched. Cells we could not source are
omitted, not guessed. Task-queue options are not compared per component; they get one Queue column.

**Names are not canonical.** The bold text in each cell is the product's own name for the
capability, taken from its docs. The same stage goes by different names in different factories.

### Task-queue options

| Product | Queue | Demoable | Where it takes it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linear | **Issues, Projects, Cycles**: Issues are Linear's fundamental unit of work; Projects group issues around a shared outcome, and Cycles are a team's repeating planning period. ([source](https://linear.app/docs/conceptual-model), as of 2026-10-10) | unknown | unknown |
| Jira | **Work items (formerly issues)**: Work items are the building blocks of Jira and can represent a story, bug, task or another work type. ([source](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-software-cloud/docs/what-is-an-issue/), as of 2026-10-10) | unknown | unknown |
| GitHub Issues | **Issues, sub-issues, Projects**: Issues track bugs, features and ideas; sub-issues add hierarchies between issues, and Projects is integrated with issues to plan and track a team's work. ([source](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/learning-about-issues/about-issues), as of 2026-10-10) | unknown | unknown |

## Omitted cells

- Devin / A person approves or edits first: Pages checked: Ask Devin, Linear, Jira, Using Playbooks, gallery bulk-plan-backlog and prd-to-tickets (docs.devin.ai). They describe a person working with Devin in conversation or Devin posting plan comments with open questions, but none states whether a person must approve or edit the plan before work starts.
- GitHub Copilot coding agent / Tasks outlive the chat: Pages checked (docs.github.com): Research, plan and iterate; Copilot CLI autopilot; Copilot on GitHub.com; Best practices; Dynamic workflows. They say the plan is shown in the conversation or executed by the same session; none says it is saved as a file or tracker items.
- GitHub Copilot coding agent / Criteria and dependencies in them: Pages checked (docs.github.com): Research, plan and iterate; Copilot CLI autopilot; Best practices; improve-a-project tutorial. None says a plan is split into tasks carrying acceptance criteria or dependencies (the tutorial has the person check criteria on issues Copilot creates from findings, which is not plan output).
- Cursor / Criteria and dependencies in them: Pages checked (cursor.com): Plan Mode docs and help, Agent overview, Prompting agents, Agentic coding help, Multi-agent help, Projects. None says plan steps carry acceptance criteria. Multi-agent help says Build in Parallel keeps dependent steps in order but not how dependencies are written.

## Updating

1. Edit `landscape/matrix.json`. Every populated cell needs `name` (the product's own term,
   or the literal `unknown` if its docs give none), `summary` (a paraphrase of the page),
   `sourceUrl` (https, on a host listed in the product's `allowedHosts`), `asOf`
   (`YYYY-MM-DD`, the day you fetched the page), and `short` (at most 8 words, the text a
   slide cell shows; name the surface when a product has two). Factories carry one cell per
   component; task-queue products carry one `queue` cell.
2. `demoable` and `destination` need the same source and date unless they are explicitly
   `unknown` (`kind: "unknown"` / `summary: "unknown"`).
3. If you cannot find a first-party page that supports a cell, replace it with
   `{ "omitted": "reason" }`; the reason names the pages checked. Never fill a cell from memory.
4. Run `bun scripts/render-landscape.ts` to regenerate this file, then
   `bun scripts/check-landscape.ts` (also run in CI) to validate.
